title: RFID Coin Tag — Small Disc HF/UHF Token for Tool, Asset and Loyalty Identification
summary: RFID coin tags pack an HF (ISO 14443 / ISO 15693) or UHF (ISO 18000-63 / GS1 EPC Gen2v2) chip into a 10-30 mm disc, 2-4 mm thick, with epoxy or ABS encapsulation rated IP67/IP68. They suit tool-crib and FOD programmes, calibrated-instrument tracking, gym / locker / laundry loops, loyalty and cashless-payment tokens, amusement / leisure tap-points, and product-authentication anchors — the cases where space on the host item is the binding constraint and a pocket-size disc is the cleanest mechanical fit.

brief.label: Form factor
items: Disc 10-30 mm diameter × 2-4 mm thick — pocket-scale token, 0.8-3.5 g typical mass.
Optional 3-5 mm ferrite spacer lamination for on-metal UHF performance without changing the disc footprint.

brief.label: Air interface envelope
items: HF 13.56 MHz — ISO 14443 Type A/B (MIFARE Classic 1K, MIFARE DESFire EV3, NTAG 424 DNA) or ISO 15693 (I-CODE SLIX2).
UHF 860-960 MHz — ISO 18000-63 / GS1 EPC Gen2v2 ({chip:impinj-m730:name} / M750, {chip:nxp-ucode-9:name}).

brief.label: Housing and durability
items: Epoxy-encapsulated disc or injection-moulded ABS / PC disc with ultrasonic weld seam.
IP67 (HF authentication) or IP68 (laundry, aquatic leisure) ingress rating, -25 °C to +85 °C service.

brief.label: Attach methods
items: 3M VHB adhesive (3M 4910F / 5952) to non-porous host surfaces.
M3 / M4 through-hole screw mount via central bore (tool handles, gauges).

brief.label: Read range
items: HF contactless tap — 0-40 mm against phone / reader head.
UHF in free space 0.5-2 m; with ferrite spacer on steel tool body 0.3-1.5 m.

brief.label: Crypto options (HF)
items: NTAG 424 DNA SUN message with CMAC — 1-tap authentication of consumer product / loyalty token.
MIFARE DESFire EV3 AES mutual auth for staff tokens and regulated cashless wallets.

brief.label: Tool-crib / FOD use case
items: Tool-return handshake at portal ≤ 100 ms per tool; batch read 20-40 tools on a tray.
Ties into aerospace FOD programmes where 100% tool accountability is required before closing a panel.

brief.label: Loyalty / cashless use case
items: Gym / spa / pool / locker token; amusement-park pay-per-ride cashless wallet; laundry-room wash-cycle credit.
Tap-time budget ≤ 300 ms including reader auth + POS round trip.

brief.label: Regulatory / conformance envelope
items: FCC Part 15.225 (HF) and Part 15.247 / 15.249 (UHF); RED 2014/53/EU; ISED RSS-210 / RSS-247.
Payment-adjacent tokens respect PCI PTS domain separation — the coin does not carry cardholder data, it addresses a tokenised wallet at the POS.

brief.label: Materials compliance
items: ABS / PC housing halogen-free; REACH SVHC screen; RoHS 3 (2015/863) compliance on chip + antenna foil + housing.
Food-contact-incidental grade epoxy available for hospitality and kitchen-tool variants (FDA 21 CFR 175.300).

brief.label: Integration / encoding
items: Factory TID is read-only per ISO 18000-63; EPC / NDEF payload locked with lock / permalock command after WMS encode.
EPCIS 2.0 commissioning event writes GIAI / GRAI / SGTIN or token-ID into ERP on first read.

heroPoints: Disc 10-30 mm × 2-4 mm — fits on hand tools, calibrated instruments, loyalty tokens and small product housings where larger tag geometries do not fit.
ISO 14443 + ISO 15693 + ISO 18000-63 / GS1 Gen2v2 covered in the same form factor — one SKU family answers tool-crib FOD, cashless leisure and product-authentication in one catalogue.
IP68 epoxy or ABS disc survives tool-crib abuse, 80 °C commercial dish-wash and pool-chemistry exposure without antenna delamination.

sections.title: Why pocket-scale assets are the hardest items to keep track of
bullets: Hand tools, calibration instruments, gauges, jigs and fixtures fit in a pocket — they are the most frequently lost, misplaced and borrowed-without-return items in any industrial operation, with 10-15% annual tool-loss rates routinely reported in manufacturing and MRO.
Barcode labels on hand tools are destroyed within days by grease, abrasion and solvent exposure, making barcode tool-tracking unreliable in the tool crib.
Manual check-out with barcode scanning imposes 30-60 s per transaction; workers bypass the system to save time, so 40-60 % of tool movements go unrecorded.

Calibration-controlled instruments must be kept inside their calibration date and used only on the correct job; losing the chain of custody creates quality escapes and audit findings under ISO 9001 7.1.5 / ISO 17025.
Aerospace FOD programmes require 100 % tool accountability before closing an aircraft panel — a single unaccounted tool can ground an aircraft and trigger a costly inspection.
Leisure / loyalty operators face a parallel problem: paper tickets and magstripe cards fail in wet, chlorinated, high-throughput environments where a sealed coin token is the natural answer.

sections.title: HF vs UHF coin tag — picking the right air interface
bullets: HF ISO 14443 / ISO 15693 — tap-to-authenticate against a reader head or smartphone; NTAG 424 DNA SUN message delivers 1-tap consumer authentication with a per-tap CMAC tied to the factory UID.
UHF ISO 18000-63 / GS1 EPC Gen2v2 — 0.5-2 m free-space read, portal-scan of a full tool tray in one sweep; suits tool-crib FOD and MRO rack accountability.
On-metal hand tools need a UHF-on-metal coin with integrated ferrite spacer, or an HF-label variant that is less sensitive to the metal boundary.
Cashless leisure and loyalty prefer HF (simpler phone tap path, mature POS integration) while high-throughput asset tracking prefers UHF (hands-free portal reads).
Dual-interface coins carry both an HF and a UHF antenna on the same 30 mm disc, at the cost of a slightly thicker 4 mm profile and a roughly 20-30 % free-space UHF read-range reduction.

sections.title: Where RFID coin tags earn their place in the catalogue
bullets: Tool-crib and FOD — hand tools, calibrated instruments, torque wrenches, jigs and fixtures; aerospace 100 % tool accountability before panel close-out, with a ≤ 100 ms per-tag portal handshake.
Calibration-controlled inventory — gauges, micrometers, hardness-testers; each coin carries the asset-ID which the asset-management system ties to current calibration certificate and next-due date.
Healthcare small-asset — endoscopes, surgical trays, patient-side instruments; coin mounted through a tray attachment bore or epoxied to an instrument handle; UDI traceability under 21 CFR Part 830.
Leisure / loyalty / cashless — gym / spa / pool locker tokens, amusement-park pay-per-ride wallets, laundromat wash-cycle credits; HF tap against POS; PCI PTS domain separation kept clean.
Product-authentication anchor — NTAG 424 DNA SUN coin glued under a product label or inside a luxury-goods hang-tag; each consumer tap writes a per-tap CMAC into the brand-protection backend.
Event and access — conference delegate token, amusement multi-day pass, staff / volunteer credential; disc can be strung on a lanyard or fixed to a wristband bracket.

dataHighlight.heading: FOD and tool-crib capture once the coin sits on every hand tool
dataHighlight.text: Industry tool-crib data consistently reports 10-15 % annual tool-loss rates under manual logging. With an IP68 RFID coin glued or screwed onto each hand tool and a UHF portal at the crib door, the capture rate for check-out / check-in events rises above 99 % and annual tool-loss drops to low single-digit percent, because the handshake happens automatically and there is no incentive to bypass the system.
dataHighlight.source: Aerospace and MRO tool-control programme case studies summarised in Boeing and Airbus FOD-prevention guidance and in SAE AIR5562 Foreign Object Damage / Debris (FOD) Prevention Program, 2022.

sections.title: How to roll out an RFID coin programme without breaking calibration, payment or privacy
bullets: Pick the air interface first: UHF on-metal coin for tool-crib / FOD, HF NTAG 424 DNA for consumer authentication, HF MIFARE DESFire EV3 for staff / cashless wallets, HF I-CODE SLIX2 for library / document loops.
Lock the factory TID and permalock the EPC / NDEF payload after WMS / POS encode — an unlocked coin is the single biggest failure mode in a brand-protection or cashless pilot.
Mind PCI PTS domain separation — the coin carries a token-ID that addresses a wallet at the POS; it does not carry cardholder data. Keep the authorisation path inside a PCI-scoped reader.
Register tool-crib coins against ISO 9001 7.1.5 / ISO 17025 calibration records so the EPCIS event stream is the single source of truth for next-due date and last-used job.

For consumer-facing loyalty / authentication, publish a privacy notice covering the tap-event payload (ID + timestamp + venue) under GDPR Art. 13 or an equivalent regional rule; data minimisation is straightforward because the coin does not carry PII.
Plan for loss — a lost coin costs USD 1-3 in the batch; the loss of the host tool, instrument or wallet value is what the coin exists to prevent.

items.label: Week 1 — profile choice
items.text: Run a matrix of candidate host items (tool, instrument, token, product) against read-range and authentication needs; lock air interface (HF / UHF / dual) and chip choice (MIFARE DESFire EV3 / NTAG 424 DNA / I-CODE SLIX2 / {chip:impinj-m750:name}) per SKU.

items.label: Weeks 2-3 — encoding workflow
items.text: Stand up POS / WMS encode bench that writes a locked EPC / NDEF, issues a factory lock / permalock, and commits an EPCIS commissioning event to ERP. Validate the 100 % lock rate on the first 5,000 coins before scale-up.

items.label: Weeks 4-6 — portal + POS deployment
items.text: Deploy UHF portal at the tool-crib door (tool-FOD) or HF readers at leisure POS. Tune antenna power so portal reads the full tray with < 0.5 % miss rate and no read-leak through the wall to the adjacent zone.

items.label: Weeks 7-10 — compliance wrap
items.text: Tie the coin ID to ISO 9001 7.1.5 / ISO 17025 calibration records for the tool case, or to the PCI-scoped wallet for the cashless-leisure case. File DPIA / Art. 13 notice for the consumer-authentication case. Bring in internal audit for the first quarterly close.

items.label: Month 4+ — scale and reuse
items.text: Operating context extends to tool-crib, FOD, cashless-leisure and product-authentication programmes — review periodicity, refresh windows and audit obligations vary by vertical and are documented per estate. scale from pilot cell to 100,000 – 5,000,000 coins across multi-site operations, with EPCIS event stream → ERP → CMMS / POS / brand-protection analytics tying each coin to an asset, wallet or product identity.

faq.question: Is the RFID coin tag waterproof enough for pool and laundry use?
faq.answer: Yes — the epoxy-encapsulated variant is rated IP68 per IEC 60529 and tolerates -25 °C to +85 °C plus typical chlorinated pool chemistry and 80 °C commercial dish-wash or laundry cycles. For continuous chemical exposure beyond that envelope, a 316L stainless or PTFE-overmoulded variant is available.

faq.question: Can a coin tag carry cashless-payment credit?
faq.answer: Not directly. The coin carries a token-ID that addresses a wallet at the POS; the wallet holds the balance inside a PCI PTS-scoped system. This domain separation keeps the coin outside PCI DSS scope while still delivering a 300 ms tap-to-pay leisure experience.

faq.question: How do I pick between HF and UHF for a loyalty / authentication programme?
faq.answer: HF (ISO 14443 / ISO 15693) is the natural choice when the customer taps a phone or POS head at 0-40 mm range and you want NTAG 424 DNA-grade authentication with a per-tap CMAC. UHF (ISO 18000-63 / GS1 Gen2v2) is the natural choice when you need handsfree portal reads at 0.5-2 m — FOD, tool-crib, MRO rack accountability. Dual-interface coins exist and cost a modest read-range penalty.
